title.en: Unlink the k-th node from the back
title.es: Desconectar el k-ésimo nodo desde el final

prompt.en:
Write `remove_kth_from_end(head, k)`: remove the `k`-th node counting from the end of a singly linked list (`k = 1` is the last node) and return the first node of the result, or `None` if nothing is left. The list has at least one node and `1 ≤ k ≤` its length. Each `ListNode` has `val` and `next`.

Aim for a single pass, without counting the nodes first, and unlink the node instead of building a new list.

The tests call the provided `run_remove_kth_from_end(values, k)`, which builds the list from `values` and returns the values of the list you return.
prompt.es:
Escribe `remove_kth_from_end(head, k)`: quita el `k`-ésimo nodo contando desde el final de una lista enlazada simple (`k = 1` es el último nodo) y devuelve el primer nodo del resultado, o `None` si no queda nada. La lista tiene al menos un nodo y `1 ≤ k ≤` su largo. Cada `ListNode` tiene `val` y `next`.

Apunta a una sola pasada, sin contar antes los nodos, y desconecta el nodo en vez de construir una lista nueva.

Los tests llaman a `run_remove_kth_from_end(values, k)`, ya incluida: construye la lista a partir de `values` y devuelve los valores de la lista que devuelves tú.

hints.en: Use two pointers with a fixed gap of `k` nodes: when the front one reaches the last node, the back one sits just before the node to remove.
hints.es: Usa dos punteros separados por `k` nodos: cuando el de adelante llega al último nodo, el de atrás queda justo antes del nodo que hay que quitar.

hints.en: Start both at a dummy node placed before the head. Then removing the first node (`k` equal to the length) is the same move as any other: `trail.next = trail.next.next`.
hints.es: Parte ambos en un nodo dummy puesto antes de la cabeza. Así, quitar el primer nodo (`k` igual al largo) es el mismo movimiento que cualquier otro: `trail.next = trail.next.next`.

solution:
# --- your code ---
def remove_kth_from_end(head: "ListNode | None", k: int) -> "ListNode | None":
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)            # a node before the head: removing the head is no special case
    lead = trail = dummy
    for _ in range(k):                   # open a gap of k nodes
        lead = lead.next
    while lead.next is not None:         # slide the gap until lead is on the last node
        lead = lead.next
        trail = trail.next
    trail.next = trail.next.next         # trail sits just before the k-th node from the end
    return dummy.next


# --- provided: do not edit ---
class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


def build_list(values: list[int]) -> ListNode | None:
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    return head


def to_nodes(head: ListNode | None, limit: int) -> list[ListNode]:
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        if len(out) == limit:
            raise ValueError("the result has more nodes than the input: is there a cycle?")
        out.append(head)
        head = head.next
    return out


def run_remove_kth_from_end(values: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    head = build_list(values)
    given = to_nodes(head, len(values))
    left = to_nodes(remove_kth_from_end(head, k), len(values))
    if not {id(n) for n in left} <= {id(n) for n in given}:
        raise ValueError("unlink one node instead of building a new list")
    return [n.val for n in left]

explain.en: Start both pointers at a dummy node before the head and move `lead` `k` nodes ahead. Then advance both until `lead` is on the last node: the gap is still `k`, so `trail` stops right before the `k`-th node from the end, and one link skips it. One pass, O(1) memory. The dummy matters when `k` equals the length: the node to remove is the head, and with nothing before it you need a special case. Return `dummy.next`, not `head`.
explain.es: Parte ambos punteros en un nodo dummy antes de la cabeza y adelanta `lead` `k` nodos. Luego avanza ambos hasta que `lead` quede en el último nodo: la distancia sigue siendo `k`, así que `trail` se detiene justo antes del `k`-ésimo nodo desde el final, y un enlace se lo salta. Una pasada, O(1) de memoria. El dummy importa cuando `k` es igual al largo: el nodo a quitar es la cabeza, y sin nada antes necesitas un caso especial. Devuelve `dummy.next`, no `head`.
